subject: AWS Marketplace: elevator copy + usage metric clarifications for Acme Analytics listing
messages:

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Quick follow up: AWS listing elevator + usage math

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We started sketching the AWS listing and have two things blocking us before we submit:

1) Elevator / hero line — we want something concise for the top of the product page that sells the cost and latency benefits for inference-heavy workloads. Can you share a tight 1-2 sentence option that mentions predictable throughput and cost-per-inference?

2) Usage metric clarity — AWS is asking how we intend to meter the product (tokens vs inference-units vs concurrent-hours). Our billing is a hybrid: per-request token-ish unit with a small concurrency surcharge. Need Redwood language that maps to Marketplace SKU definitions so the finance team can build the private offer.

I attached our current one-pager for context. Appreciate short, concrete responses — procurement wants to start penning the PO next week.

Thanks,
Eve
Eve Johnson
Head of Data Platform | Acme Analytics

Hi Eve — thanks for the clear asks. See answers inline and a couple of draft hero lines below.

On Fri, Aug 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Eve Johnson wrote:
> 1) Elevator / hero line — we want something concise for the top of the product page that sells the cost and latency benefits for inference-heavy workloads.

Draft hero candidates (short):
- "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable cost and sub-100ms tail latency for production apps."
- "Run low-latency LLM inference at scale — predictable pricing, dedicated throughput, no surprises."
- "Cost-conscious, SLA-backed inference for product teams — dedicated capacity and smart caching."

Pick one and I’ll tailor the subhead (3-4 lines) to emphasize routing/fallback and cache benefits.

> 2) Usage metric clarity — AWS is asking how we intend to meter the product (tokens vs inference-units vs concurrent-hours).

Short answer (for Marketplace):
- Primary SKU: "inference-unit" measured per 1,000 generated tokens equivalent (maps to tokenized output + model compute).
- Secondary SKU: "concurrency-hour" applies when reserved pooled concurrency exceeds burst levels (flat hourly surcharge).
- Line-item: cache hits are billed at 10% of an inference-unit to reflect lower compute.

Ben / Karthik / Lauren — can you confirm the above is safe to surface to AWS and whether there are any legal/pricing constraints we should hide from the public listing? Also flag if the cache hit discount needs an exact % change.

Action items:
- Eve: pick hero line and I’ll produce a 2-line subhead + 3 bullets of customer benefits we can paste into the Seller Central form.
- Karthik: technical confirmation on mapping tokens -> inference-unit and the cache policy language.
- Ben / Lauren: marketing polish + final CTA copy for the product page.

Thanks — attaching the mock hero artwork for layout reference.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow up: AWS listing elevator + usage math

Jonas / team — technical notes on the billing mapping and a couple of suggested edits for clarity.

Short technical mapping:
- "Inference-unit" = compute-weighted token unit. We normalize across models by a model-class multiplier (e.g., small=1.0, medium=2.5, large=5.0). The marketplace SKU will state "per 1,000 inference-units" to keep numbers tidy.
- "Cache hit" policy: We should avoid promising an exact percentage publicly. Suggesting "reduced compute billing for cached responses (subject to policy)" in the public listing and leaving the specific discount in the private offer attachment. AWS legal prefers vaguer public language.
- "Concurrency-hour" is OK as a labeled surcharge for reserved burst capacity; call it "reserved throughput hour" to avoid confusion with instance-hours.

Attached a simple CSV with examples mapping sample calls to SKU math (pricing_matrix_au_vs_tokens.csv).

Copy tweak for hero candidates: change candidate 2 to: "Run low-latency LLM inference at scale — predictable per-inference pricing and dedicated throughput."

Also: include a short FAQ line on the product page: "How are requests billed?" -> "Requests are billed against a standardized inference-unit. Reserved throughput and cache behavior are documented in the private offer. Contact sales for a tailored pricing model."

If that sounds good I’ll update the Drive doc and we can hand to procurement.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Platform Billing | Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_matrix_au_vs_tokens.csv (CSV, 15KB)
